title: Landing readiness check
description: Before landing, merge checks review stage, close-out evidence, lane identity, claim, dirty files, blocking QA, post-deploy QA and landing-route gates. The read-only --check uses the same checks. An item one declared edge before review is moved into review by the merge, running that stage's gates; --check asks the stage's database-claim prose gate read-only and reports a prose-vs-claim mismatch as a blocker, and its merge_will note names the stage's other gates, which only the merge's own transition evaluates. Past review, once the target is proven to contain the landing, close-out skips review-entry lane checks. The run writer observes the start commit when available; the latest completed pass on an effective item requirement counts without commit comparison. Newer failures or incomplete runs, changed configuration or target, missing subject proof and human review still block. Required merge-queue CI tests the final commit. Source-observed; not yet verified-live. Missing-proof refusals name the requested action: merge checks say merge, while lifecycle checks name the transition and target status. The steering report uses the landing stamp and merge receipt for landed PRs. Unresolved PRs, including open re-land attempts, get one GitHub transport attempt per report without retry backoff. A failed read stays unreadable for that report, and the next report tries again. Other landing callers retain their retry policy. Red required-check readbacks list each failed check and URL once, followed by recovery guidance; the merge entry refusal keeps its complete diagnosis. Live landing readiness reads auto-merge, the PR queue entry and required checks in one GraphQL projection per distinct PR. An enqueued PR remains in flight after GitHub consumes auto-merge; a failed PR read leaves the queue entry unreadable. Fleet reports never read the branch queue for landing readiness. The --skip-status flag postpones only done: merge still moves the item to release and releases its work claim. Merge each step of multi-step work as its own item. Before actual merge readiness, a local lane HEAD differing from its recorded candidate is recorded and re-read; a recording failure names the cause and asks the operator to retry the merge. The read-only check names both revisions when the selected local lane HEAD differs from its record. Text says the merge will record the stale lane head, and JSON reports the same comparison in merge_will. Standalone retry close-out rechecks post-push CI on the landing commit, and failed publication reports its push error before ancestry proof. Queue --check also uses the landing composition and unchanged failed-train gates. It reads queue members and an existing pull request without creating or publishing one; unreadable queue or PR inputs are merge_will notes, while known admission refusals block. Without an existing PR the failed-train gate waits for the merge. Standalone push checks gate close-out only when ci_workflow_file is declared or its declaration cannot be read. With no declaration, close-out samples push checks once, records observed failures as receipt evidence and warns without gating.
